lines.text: After Ramakrishna's passing, his young disciples took a crumbling house at Baranagore, said to be haunted.
lines.ph: ˈæftɚ ɹˌɑːməkɹˈɪʃnəz pˈæsɪŋ, hɪz jˈʌŋ dɪsˈaɪpəlz tˈʊk ɐ kɹˈʌmblɪŋ hˈaʊs æt bˈɑːɹənəɡˌɔːɹ, sˈɛd təbi hˈɔːntᵻd.

lines.text: Some days there was rice but no salt. For months they lived on rice, salt, and boiled leaves.
lines.ph: sˌʌm dˈeɪz ðɛɹwˌʌz ɹˈaɪs bˌʌt nˈoʊ sˈɔlt. fɔːɹ mˈʌnθs ðeɪ lˈɪvd ˌɔn ɹˈaɪs, sˈɔlt, ænd bˈɔɪld lˈiːvz.

lines.text: And they argued for hours: Kant, Hegel, Mill and Spencer, against the six systems of India.
lines.ph: ænd ðeɪ ˈɑːɹɡjuːd fɔːɹ ˈaʊɚz: kˈɑːnt, hˈeɪɡəl, mˈɪl ænd spˈɛnsɚ, ɐɡˈɛnst ðə sˈɪks sˈɪstəmz ʌv ˈɪndiə.

lines.text: One day Naren would prove that God was a myth. The next, that God was the only reality.
lines.ph: wˈʌn dˈeɪ nəɹˈeɪn wʊd pɹˈuːv ðæt ɡˈɑːd wʌzɐ mˈɪθ. ðə nˈɛkst, ðæt ɡˈɑːd wʌzðɪ ˈoʊnli ɹɪˈælᵻɾi.

lines.text: How had the Upanishads reached German philosophy at all?
lines.ph: hˌaʊ hˈæd ðə uːpˈʌnɪʃədz ɹˈiːtʃt dʒˈɜːmən fɪlˈɑːsəfi æɾ ˈɔːl?

lines.text: The Mughal prince Dara Shikoh had them translated into Persian.
lines.ph: ðˈə mˈuːɡəl pɹˈɪns dˈɑːɹɑː ʃˈɪkoʊ hˌædðɛm tɹænslˈeɪɾᵻd ˌɪntʊ pˈɜːʒən.

lines.text: A Latin version reached Europe, and Schopenhauer read it. His philosophy, Vivekananda said, was moulded by it.
lines.ph: ɐ lˈætɪn vˈɜːʒən ɹˈiːtʃt jˈʊɹɹəp, ˈænd ʃˈoʊpənhaʊɚ ɹˈiːd ɪt. hɪz fɪlˈɑːsəfi, vɪvˌeɪkɑːnˈʌndə sˈɛd, wʌz mˈoʊldᵻd baɪ ɪt.

lines.text: Next to him, he said, the philosophy of Kant also shows traces of the Upanishads.
lines.ph: nˈɛkst tə hˌɪm, hiː sˈɛd, ðə fɪlˈɑːsəfi ʌv kˈɑːnt ˈɔːlsoʊ ʃˈoʊz tɹˈeɪsᵻz ʌvðə uːpˈʌnɪʃədz.

lines.text: Two ancient peoples, he said, looked for the infinite in different directions.
lines.ph: tˈuː ˈeɪntʃənt pˈiːpəlz, hiː sˈɛd, lˈʊkt fɚðɪ ˈɪnfɪnət ɪn dˈɪfɹənt dᵻɹˈɛkʃənz.

lines.text: The Greeks, surrounded by beauty, studied the outer infinite. The macrocosm.
lines.ph: ðə ɡɹˈiːks, sɚɹˈaʊndᵻd baɪ bjˈuːɾi, stˈʌdid ðɪ ˈaʊɾɚɹ ˈɪnfɪnət. ðə mˈækɹəkˌɑːzəm.

lines.text: India, surrounded by the sublime, studied the inner infinite. The microcosm.
lines.ph: ˈɪndiə, sɚɹˈaʊndᵻd baɪ ðə sʌblˈaɪm, stˈʌdid ðɪ ˈɪnɚɹ ˈɪnfɪnət. ðə mˈaɪkɹoʊkˌɑːzəm.

lines.text: Neither needed to borrow from the other. But if they compared notes, both would gain.
lines.ph: nˈiːðɚ nˈiːdᵻd tə bˈɑːɹoʊ fɹʌmðɪ ˈʌðɚ. bˌʌt ɪf ðeɪ kəmpˈɛɹd nˈoʊts, bˈoʊθ wʊd ɡˈeɪn.

lines.text: In eighteen ninety, Naren left with a staff and a begging bowl, and the dust of India swallowed him.
lines.ph: ɪn ˈeɪtiːn nˈaɪnti, nəɹˈeɪn lˈɛft wɪð ɐ stˈæf ænd ɐ bˈɛɡɪŋ bˈoʊl, ænd ðə dˈʌst ʌv ˈɪndiə swˈɔloʊd hˌɪm.

lines.text: Varanasi, Vrindavan, the Himalayas, Rajputana, Gujarat, Mysore, Travancore, and at last, Kanyakumari.
lines.ph: vɑːɹˈɑːnəsi, vɹˈɪndɑːvən, ðə hˌɪməlˈeɪəz, ɹˌɑːdʒpʊtˈɑːnə, ɡˌʊdʒɐɹˈæt, mˈaɪsoːɹ, tɹˈævəŋkɔːɹ, ænd æt lˈæst, kˌʌnjɑːkʊmˈɑːɹi.

lines.text: In Madras a disciple marvelled at his range: from the Rig Veda to Kant and Hegel, from Yoga to a modern laboratory.
lines.ph: ɪn mədɹˈɑːs ɐ dɪsˈaɪpəl mˈɑːɹvəld æt hɪz ɹˈeɪndʒ: fɹʌmðˈə ɹˈɪɡ vˈeɪdə tˈuː kˈɑːnt ˈænd hˈeɪɡəl, fɹʌm jˈoʊɡə tʊ ɐ mˈɑːdɚn lˈæbɹətˌɔːɹi.

lines.text: On the thirty-first of May, eighteen ninety-three, he sailed from Bombay for the West.
lines.ph: ɔnðə θˈɜːɾifˈɜːst ʌv mˈeɪ, ˈeɪtiːn nˈaɪntiθɹˈiː, hiː sˈeɪld fɹʌm bˈɑːmbeɪ fɚðə wˈɛst.

lines.text: Back in Calcutta, he named the German he trusted least: Hegel.
lines.ph: bˈæk ɪn kælkˈʌɾə, hiː nˈeɪmd ðə dʒˈɜːmən hiː tɹˈʌstᵻd lˈiːst: hˈeɪɡəl.

lines.text: Hegel's idea, he said, is that the Absolute is only chaos, and the individual form is greater. The world is greater than the non-world.
lines.ph: hˈeɪɡəlz aɪdˈiə, hiː sˈɛd, ɪz ðætðɪ ˈæbsəlˌuːt ɪz ˈoʊnli kˈeɪɑːs, ænd ðɪ ˌɪndᵻvˈɪdʒuːəl fˈɔːɹm ɪz ɡɹˈeɪɾɚ. ðə wˈɜːld ɪz ɡɹˈeɪɾɚ ðɐn ðə nˈɑːnwˈɜːld.

lines.text: India's answer: every manifestation is a vain attempt of the unmanifested to show itself, like the sun trying to reflect itself in little mud puddles.
lines.ph: ˈɪndiəz ˈænsɚ: ˈɛvɹi mˌænɪfɪstˈeɪʃən ɪz ɐ vˈeɪn ɐtˈɛmpt ʌvðɪ ʌnmˈænɪfˌɛstᵻd tə ʃˈoʊ ɪtsˈɛlf, lˈaɪk ðə sˈʌn tɹˈaɪɪŋ tə ɹᵻflˈɛkt ɪtsˈɛlf ɪn lˈɪɾəl mˈʌd pˈʌdəlz.

lines.text: After a time it beats a retreat to where it came from. That, he said, is renunciation, the beginning of religion.
lines.ph: ˈæftɚɹ ɐ tˈaɪm ɪt bˈiːts ɐ ɹᵻtɹˈiːt tʊ wˌɛɹ ɪt kˈeɪm fɹʌm. ðˈæt, hiː sˈɛd, ɪz ɹᵻnˌʌnsɪˈeɪʃən, ðə bɪɡˈɪnɪŋ ʌv ɹᵻlˈɪdʒən.

lines.text: In eighteen ninety-six, Professor Paul Deussen invited him to Kiel. Deussen was a disciple of Schopenhauer, and a follower of Kant.
lines.ph: ɪn ˈeɪtiːn nˈaɪntisˈɪks, pɹəfˈɛsɚ pˈɔːl dˈɔɪsən ɪnvˈaɪɾᵻd hˌɪm tuː kˈiːl. dˈɔɪsən wʌzɐ dɪsˈaɪpəl ʌv ʃˈoʊpənhaʊɚ, ænd ɐ fˈɑːloʊɚɹ ʌv kˈɑːnt.

lines.text: He spoke Sanskrit, and called the Vedanta one of the most majestic structures of the human mind.
lines.ph: hiː spˈoʊk sˈænskɹɪt, ænd kˈɔːld ðə veɪdˈɑːntə wˈʌn ʌvðə mˈoʊst mɐdʒˈɛstɪk stɹˈʌktʃɚz ʌvðə hjˈuːmən mˈaɪnd.

lines.text: Once, absorbed in a book of poems, the Swami did not hear his host. Then he recited the verses back to him.
lines.ph: wˈʌns, ɐbsˈoːɹbd ɪn ɐ bˈʊk ʌv pˈoʊᵻmz, ðˈə swˈɑːmi dɪdnˌɑːt hˈɪɹ hɪz hˈoʊst. ðˈɛn hiː ɹᵻsˈaɪɾᵻd ðə vˈɜːsᵻz bˈæk tə hˌɪm.

lines.text: Deussen foresaw India becoming the spiritual leader of the nations.
lines.ph: dˈɔɪsən fˈɔːɹsɔː ˈɪndiə bᵻkˈʌmɪŋ ðə spˈɪɹɪtʃˌuːəl lˈiːdɚɹ ʌvðə nˈeɪʃənz.

lines.text: In London he gave three lectures on Maya. Some listeners, it is said, were moved to tears.
lines.ph: ɪn lˈʌndən hiː ɡˈeɪv θɹˈiː lˈɛktʃɚz ˈɔn mˈɑːjɑː. sˌʌm lˈɪsənɚz, ɪɾ ɪz sˈɛd, wɜː mˈuːvd tə tˈɪɹz.

lines.text: A white-haired philosopher told him: you have spoken splendidly, but you have told us nothing new.
lines.ph: ɐ wˈaɪthˈɛɹd fɪlˈɑːsəfɚ tˈoʊld hˌɪm: juː hæv spˈoʊkən splˈɛndɪdli, bˌʌt juː hæv tˈoʊld ˌʌs nˈʌθɪŋ nˈuː.

lines.text: He answered: Sir, I have told you the Truth. And the Truth is as old as the hills.
lines.ph: hiː ˈænsɚd: sˈɜː, aɪ hæv tˈoʊld juː ðə tɹˈuːθ. ænd ðə tɹˈuːθ ɪz æz ˈoʊld æz ðə hˈɪlz.

lines.text: If I have told it in words that make you think, and live up to your thinking, do I not do well?
lines.ph: ɪf aɪ hæv tˈoʊld ɪɾ ɪn wˈɜːdz ðæt mˌeɪk juː θˈɪŋk, ænd lˈaɪv ˌʌp tə jʊɹ θˈɪŋkɪŋ, dˈuː aɪ nˌɑːt dˈuː wˈɛl?

lines.text: In June eighteen ninety-nine he sailed again, with Sister Nivedita, on the Golconda.
lines.ph: ɪn dʒˈuːn ˈeɪtiːn nˈaɪntinˈaɪn hiː sˈeɪld ɐɡˈɛn, wɪð sˈɪstɚ nɪvˈeɪdɪtɑː, ɔnðˈə ɡɑːlkˈɑːndə.

lines.text: At Madras, plague kept every Indian passenger aboard. The monsoon tossed them for ten days to Aden.
lines.ph: æt mədɹˈɑːs, plˈeɪɡ kˈɛpt ˈɛvɹi ˈɪndiən pˈæsɪndʒɚɹ ɐbˈoːɹd. ðə mɔnsˈuːn tˈɔst ðˌɛm fɔːɹ tˈɛn dˈeɪz tʊ ˈeɪdən.

lines.text: On deck he set Kant's time, space and causation beside the Vaisheshika categories, and the logic of the Nyaya.
lines.ph: ˌɔn dˈɛk hiː sˈɛt kˈɑːnts tˈaɪm, spˈeɪs ænd kɔːsˈeɪʃən bᵻsˈaɪd ðə vaɪʃˈeɪʃɪkə kˈæɾɪɡɚɹiz, ænd ðə lˈɑːdʒɪk ʌvðə njˈɑːjə.

lines.text: One side gives priority to the outer thing, he said, the other to the inner idea. That problem has no solution.
lines.ph: wˈʌn sˈaɪd ɡˈɪvz pɹaɪˈɔːɹᵻɾi tə ðɪ ˈaʊɾɚ θˈɪŋ, hiː sˈɛd, ðɪ ˈʌðɚ tə ðɪ ˈɪnɚɹ aɪdˈiə. ðæt pɹˈɑːbləm hɐz nˈoʊ səlˈuːʃən.

lines.text: Off Sicily, Etna was in eruption, and the moon rose over the Straits of Messina.
lines.ph: ˈɔf sˈɪsɪli, ˈɛtnə wʌz ɪn ɪɹˈʌpʃən, ænd ðə mˈuːn ɹˈoʊz ˌoʊvɚ ðə stɹˈeɪts ʌv məsˈiːnə.

lines.text: Beauty, he told Nivedita, is not outside. It is already in the mind.
lines.ph: bjˈuːɾi, hiː tˈoʊld nɪvˈeɪdɪtɑː, ɪz nˌɑːt aʊtsˈaɪd. ɪɾ ɪz ɔːlɹˌɛdi ɪnðə mˈaɪnd.

lines.text: Look at these two grey squares. They are the very same grey. The surroundings make one look darker.
lines.ph: lˈʊk æt ðiːz tˈuː ɡɹˈeɪ skwˈɛɹz. ðeɪ ɑːɹ ðə vˈɛɹi sˈeɪm ɡɹˈeɪ. ðə sɚɹˈaʊndɪŋz mˌeɪk wˈʌn lˈʊk dˈɑːɹkɚ.

lines.text: Messina must thank me, he laughed. It is I who give her all her beauty.
lines.ph: məsˈiːnə mˈʌst θˈæŋk mˌiː, hiː lˈæft. ɪɾ ɪz aɪ hˌuː ɡˈɪv hɜːɹ ˈɔːl hɜː bjˈuːɾi.

lines.text: Crossing the Atlantic that August, he paced the deck under a full moon.
lines.ph: kɹˈɔsɪŋ ðɪ ɐtlˈæntɪk ðæt ˈɔːɡəst, hiː pˈeɪst ðə dˈɛk ˌʌndɚɹ ɐ fˈʊl mˈuːn.

lines.text: If all this Maya is so beautiful, he said, think of the wondrous beauty of the Reality behind it.
lines.ph: ɪf ˈɔːl ðˈɪs mˈɑːjɑː ɪz sˌoʊ bjˈuːɾifəl, hiː sˈɛd, θˈɪŋk ʌvðə wˈʌndɹəs bjˈuːɾi ʌvðə ɹɪˈælᵻɾi bᵻhˈaɪnd ɪt.

lines.text: And pointing to the sea and sky: why recite poetry, when there is the very essence of poetry?
lines.ph: ænd pˈɔɪntɪŋ tə ðə sˈiː ænd skˈaɪ: wˌaɪ ɹᵻsˈaɪt pˈoʊɪtɹi, wˌɛn ðɛɹ ɪz ðə vˈɛɹi ˈɛsəns ʌv pˈoʊɪtɹi?

lines.text: The boy who studied Kant in Calcutta had carried the question around the world.
lines.ph: ðə bˈɔɪ hˌuː stˈʌdid kˈɑːnt ɪn kælkˈʌɾə hæd kˈæɹid ðə kwˈɛstʃən ɚɹˈaʊnd ðə wˈɜːld.

lines.text: Kant showed that time, space and causation are forms of the mind. The Upanishads added: what lies beyond them is your own Self.
lines.ph: kˈɑːnt ʃˈoʊd ðæt tˈaɪm, spˈeɪs ænd kɔːsˈeɪʃən ɑːɹ fˈɔːɹmz ʌvðə mˈaɪnd. ðˈə uːpˈʌnɪʃədz ˈædᵻd: wˌʌt lˈaɪz bᵻjˌɔnd ðˌɛm ɪz jʊɹ ˈoʊn sˈɛlf.

lines.text: From whom all this universe comes out, in whom all that is born lives, and to whom all returns.
lines.ph: fɹʌm hˈuːm ˈɔːl ðɪs jˈuːnɪvˌɜːs kˈʌmz ˈaʊt, ɪn hˈuːm ˈɔːl ðæt ɪz bˈɔːɹn lˈaɪvz, ænd tə hˈuːm ˈɔːl ɹᵻtˈɜːnz.

lines.text: Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.
lines.ph: ɚɹˈaɪz, ɐwˈeɪk, ænd stˈɑːp nˌɑːt tˈɪl ðə ɡˈoʊl ɪz ɹˈiːtʃt.
